triples.evidence_text: Prednisone is a prescription corticosteroid (steroid) used to reduce inflammation, suppress an overactive immune system, and treat endocrine and metabolic disorders. Prednisone is used for a wide range of conditions, including severe allergies, asthma and COPD flare-ups, rheumatoid arthritis and other forms of arthritis, lupus, psoriasis and other skin conditions, ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, eye inflammation, some blood disorders, and low adrenal hormone levels.

Prednisone works by mimicking the effects of glucocorticoid hormones secreted naturally by our adrenal glands. Prednisone is a man-made (synthetic) version of these hormones. Prednisone is different from steroids taken to build muscle (anabolic steroids).

Prednisone tablets come in 1 mg, 2.5 mg, 5 mg, 10 mg, 20 mg, and 50 mg strengths. Prednisone 20 mg and prednisone 10 mg tablets are the strengths most often used for short courses in adults. Prednisone also comes as a delayed-release tablet (Rayos), as an oral liquid, and as a concentrated oral solution (Prednisone Intensol) that is measured with a special dropper.

qualifiers.condition: long-term use for months to years

triples.evidence_text: Taking prednisone for months or years raises the risk of osteoporosis and broken bones, muscle weakness and muscle loss, cataracts and glaucoma, diabetes, high blood pressure, Cushing's syndrome (a set of changes caused by too much steroid, including a rounded face and fat around the trunk), and adrenal suppression, where your body stops making enough of its own steroid hormones.

Children who take prednisone for a long time may grow more slowly. Your child's doctor should check their growth at regular visits.
Do not take prednisone if you have a systemic fungal infection, which is a fungal infection that has spread through your body.

Prednisone weakens your immune system. This makes it easier to get an infection; an existing infection may become worse and can reactivate an old infection, such as tuberculosis or hepatitis B. It can also hide the usual signs of infection, so an infection may be advanced before you notice it. Tell your doctor about any illness or infection you have had in the past few weeks.

qualifiers.exception: a doctor says vaccination is safe

triples.evidence_text: Do not have a live vaccine while you are taking prednisone unless your doctor says it is safe.

triples.entity_2: do not stop suddenly after use for more than a few days; gradual dose reduction may be needed
triples.evidence_text: Do not stop taking prednisone suddenly after more than a few days of treatment. Your body needs time to start making its own steroid hormones again. Your doctor will lower your dose in steps.

Take prednisone exactly as prescribed, with food or milk to protect your stomach. Your doctor will often start you on a higher dose and then lower it. Do not change your dose or stop the medicine without advice.

qualifiers.condition: dose depends on the condition and its severity

triples.section_title: What is the usual prednisone dosage?
triples.evidence_text: The usual starting dose of prednisone for adults is 5 mg to 60 mg per day, depending on the condition being treated and how severe it is.
